metadata.title: Nvidia book author said there are only two real candidates to replace Jensen Huang

content.text:
Investing.com -- Following this morning's stunning news, the question of who should lead Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) after Jensen Huang is no longer just a matter of corporate succession. It is about whether one of the world's most influential technology companies can maintain its extraordinary momentum without the man who built it.
According to Tae Kim, author of The Nvidia Way: Jensen Huang and the Making of a Tech Giant, the answer is yes. Despite the shock surrounding Huang's departure following his infidelity with two women, Kim believes Nvidia has enough leadership talent and institutional strength to thrive under a new chief executive. However, he believes the board should focus on just two candidates: Rene Haas and Ian Buck.
Rene Haas: The experienced business leader
Kim's first choice is Rene Haas, currently CEO of Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) and a former Nvidia executive.
Haas brings an attractive combination of technical understanding, executive experience and leadership skills. During his time at Arm, he has demonstrated that he can successfully manage a major technology company outside Nvidia. He also understands Nvidia's corporate culture and is already familiar with many of its senior executives.
That familiarity could prove invaluable during a leadership transition. According to Kim, former Nvidia employees have spoken highly of Haas and enjoyed working under him.
His appointment would offer continuity without simply trying to replicate Jensen Huang's leadership style. Haas has the experience and public-facing presence needed to reassure investors, employees, customers and business partners that Nvidia remains in capable hands.
Ian Buck: The technology visionary
Kim's second candidate is Ian Buck, Nvidia's vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing.
While Haas represents the experienced corporate leader, Buck represents Nvidia's technological DNA.
Buck is particularly important because he invented CUDA, Nvidia's software platform that helped transform the company's GPUs into the foundation of modern accelerated computing and AI development.
Today, he oversees products and technologies used by major cloud providers and other large customers. Kim believes Buck possesses the engineering expertise, customer relationships and respect among employees necessary to guide NVIDIA through its next phase of growth.
His appointment would send a powerful message: Nvidia's future will remain firmly rooted in technological innovation.
Jonah Alben: The executive NVIDIA cannot afford to lose
Beyond choosing a new CEO, Kim highlights another critical priority: retaining Jonah Alben, Nvidia's senior vice president of GPU engineering.
Alben plays an essential role in developing the company's GPU architecture and long-term product roadmap. Kim believes keeping him, alongside Buck, would help ensure that Nvidia's technological development continues without disruption.
In other words, the board's challenge is not simply finding a replacement for Huang. It must also protect the engineering leadership responsible for Nvidia's competitive advantage.
Nvidia's future is bigger than Jensen Huang
Kim acknowledges that Huang's departure marks the end of an extraordinary leadership era. However, he no longer believes Nvidia's success depends on one individual.
Demand for AI computing remains enormous, and the company's technology, talent and customer relationships provide a strong foundation for continued growth. Even if political pressure, regulation or changes in international markets slow expansion, Kim believes the underlying AI opportunity remains substantial.
His message to Nvidia's board is straightforward: choose Rene Haas or Ian Buck, retain Jonah Alben and preserve the company's technological direction.
The bottom line? Jensen Huang may have made Nvidia what it is today, but its future does not have to end with him. Under the right leadership, the company can continue shaping the AI revolution. For Kim, Rene Haas and Ian Buck are the two people best positioned to make that happen.
Prediction markets: Ian Buck leads the field
While Kim's assessment focuses on institutional fit and technological vision, prediction markets are already pricing in the succession race. According to data tracked and analyzed by The Action Network, which aggregates market pricing, trading activity, and historical forecasting accuracy from platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket, Ian Buck has emerged as the frontrunner:
Ian Buck (Nvidia Executive): 35.5% implied probability
Colette Kress (Interim CEO): 25.5% implied probability
Rene Haas (Arm CEO): 9.1% implied probability
Lisa Su (AMD CEO): 2.4% implied probability
Notably, market data places interim CEO Colette Kress well ahead of Kim's other preferred candidate, Rene Haas. "With Ian Buck leading our analysis at a 35.5% implied probability, followed by interim CEO Colette Kress at 25.5%, Nvidia's succession remains far from settled," Ben Mendelowitz, Prediction Markets Analyst at The Action Network, said in a statement to Investing.com, noting that the figures reflect a tension between technical expertise and leadership continuity.
Still, market sentiment can shift rapidly. Mendelowitz pointed out that prior to Huang's resignation, tracked market movements showed his exit probability surging from 13.2% to 76.6% in just three days (November 9–12), suggesting succession probabilities could swing just as quickly as new developments unfold.
